text.p: Punjab cotton remained steady in a narrow price band while Gujarat varieties bounced back from the reduced level on the local market, dealer said.
Punjab varieties were steady in a limited activity and sluggish mill buying while Gujarat cotton rose on shortage of medium and superior varieties of cotton as the end of the season drew closer.
In the spot deals Gujarat Kalyan rose by 300/400 rupees at 13,200/13,500 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).

"Punjab varieties were steady in a narrow price band amid limited activity but sentiment was subdued on reports of sliding global prices which may reduce prospects of export from India," one broker said.
In the spot deals Punjab saw-ginned was steady at 1,510/1,640 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Bengal-deshi was quiet at 880/925 rupees per maund.
The Bombay cotton market will remain closed on Friday for a Moslem festival.
